conceptName: Editing the record: audit and soft-delete

items.stem: What does an SDM-edited domain entity in DDH typically carry? Select all that apply.
items.explanation: Entities use a GUID Id, CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit fields, and a soft-delete flag — making edits attributable and reversible. They do not store passwords.

misconceptions.d: Credentials aren't stored on domain entities; auth is handled by Entra.

items.stem: A user "deletes" a record in SDM. What actually happens?

options.text: The row is marked deleted with a soft-delete flag (reversible), not physically removed
The row is permanently dropped from the database

items.explanation: SDM uses soft delete — a flag marks the record deleted, so it's recoverable and its history is preserved.

misconceptions.b: Soft delete means it isn't physically removed.
misconceptions.d: Only the single record is flagged, nothing is truncated.

items.stem: How would you answer "who last changed this record, and when?"

options.text: Read the entity's UpdatedBy field (and the AuditLog for the full who/what/when trail)
There's no way to tell — SDM keeps no record
Ask the Sync-* fleet, which stores edit history

items.explanation: The UpdatedBy audit field plus the AuditLog rows give an attributable who/what/when trail for every change.

misconceptions.b: Changes are audited via CreatedBy/UpdatedBy and the AuditLog.
misconceptions.c: The syncs propagate data; SDM's edits are audited in DDH.
misconceptions.d: Audit lives in DDH, not the browser.

items.stem: Where do the edited records and their audit trail actually live?

options.text: In the DistrictDataHub (DDH) database — SDM holds no data of its own

items.explanation: SDM is the editor; the data and its audit live in DDH. That's why the audit travels with the data the Sync-* fleet then reads.

misconceptions.b: SDM has no data store of its own; it reads/writes DDH.
misconceptions.c: Nothing authoritative is stored in the browser.
misconceptions.d: The SPA is stateless; data lives in DDH.
